sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the resolution between the two rulings regarding redemption—that Israel is redeemed only through repentance and that they will be redeemed in Nissan—by describing how the repentance at the end of exile stems from the Torah's promise rather than from the person's own self-perception, reflecting the quality of "Nissan" as a "bat" (daughter) that has nothing of its own and receives from above.

translations.translation: Based on this, we can explain the reconciliation of the two rulings regarding the redemption,
that Israel are redeemed only through repentance and that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed,
for this repentance that Israel perform at the end of their exile
[for in the exile itself,
the essential concealment and hiding of the exile is at its end],
is in a manner that is felt within them,
that this repentance they perform is not from the perspective of the self-perception of the person performing repentance51
but because the Torah promised that at the end of the exile they will repent.
The quality of Nissan,
bat,
which has nothing of its own and receives from above.
And although repentance is by his will and choice52,
as the Rambam states that ultimately Israel will repent,
the action and labor of Israel
[and unlike the awakening of repentance that comes through the proclamations from above53],
nevertheless, the performance of repentance by Israel at the end of the exile is not from their own self-perception on their own,
but because the promise of the Torah acts upon them so that they will repent.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that because the repentance at the end of exile is in the manner of "bat," which reaches the very essence of Ein Sof beyond the chain of descent, it is above order and gradation, so that Israel repent and are immediately redeemed.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this is what it means that Israel repent and are immediately redeemed32,
for when the performance of repentance is from the person himself
(who is in a state and perception that is fitting for repentance),
although repentance in general is in a manner of leap54
nevertheless there is in it some order and gradation.
For since the person is limited,
even in his leap there is order55.
First he comes to lower repentance and then to higher repentance55
until he is completely redeemed from the state
(exile)
that existed before the repentance.
And this that Israel repent at the end of their exile and are immediately redeemed,
is,
because this repentance is in the manner of bat
(from the side of the Torah's promise),
that the self-nullification of bat reaches the very essence of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent
(as above in section 5),
therefore,
the repentance of bat is above order and gradation
(above even the order of a leap).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the repentance at the end of exile combines the qualities of Tishrei (repentance from below upward by Israel's own power) and Nissan (repentance from the Torah's promise, causing immediate redemption above order), and that the ultimate purpose of the limited world created in Tishrei is to reveal within it the unlimited light of Nissan, which is why redemption will be in Nissan.

translations.translation: Now, this that the promise of the Torah acts upon the person so that he repents on his own,
is the union of Nissan and Tishrei.
For this repentance
(at the end of the exile)
that Israel perform repentance by their own power,
from below upward
[and unlike the Exodus from Egypt,
where Israel's desire to leave the impurity of Egypt and cleave to Him, blessed be He, was from the revelation from above,
therefore their exodus from Egypt was in the manner of "ki"56
the people fled57],
is the concept and virtue of Tishrei.
And this that the performance of repentance is from the side of the Torah's promise,
therefore it is in a manner of being immediately redeemed,
above order and gradation,
is the virtue of Nissan.
And as explained above
(section 2)
that the virtue of Nissan over Tishrei is that in Nissan there is the drawing down of the unlimited light.
And it can be said,
that this that specifically in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed,
even though in the repentance at the end of the exile
(through which the redemption will come)
there are both concepts and virtues,
of Nissan and of Tishrei,
is,
because the power for the union of Tishrei and Nissan in the service of man is that the ultimate58
intention in the creation of Tishrei
("In the beginning He created")
when the world was created with measure and limitation, is so that through the service of Torah and mitzvos there will be in it the revelation of Nissan
("This month is for you").
And this is that the thought to create the world was in Nissan,
for thought is the intention and purpose of the action that follows the thought
(as above in section 2),
for the intention and purpose of the creation of the world of Tishrei
(measure and limitation)
is that there be in it the revelation of Nissan which is above limitation.

But in order that the intention be completed, that even in the limited there be a revelation of the unlimited, the creation was actualized in a way that in the revelation the intention was not felt within it.
Through this a limited world was created.
And through our deeds and our service, and especially in the time of exile,
it is revealed that the inwardness
(the intention and purpose)
of the limit that was created in Tishrei is that there be in it a revelation of the unlimited light.
And this is that the performance of repentance at the end of the exile
(the action and work of man who was created in Tishrei,
limit)
is in a manner of unlimited light
(Nissan),
for through our deeds and our service it is revealed that the inner content of the limit created in Tishrei is the unlimited light of Nissan.
And this is that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed,
for then it will be revealed that even the limit of Tishrei,
its inwardness is the unlimited light of Nissan.
